newsitem.title: Sudanese rebel leaders open meeting in Eritrea.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese rebel leaders open meeting in Eritrea.

text.p: Leaders of Sudan's opposition in exile on Monday opened a four-day conference in the Eritrean capital of Asmara proclaiming a climax in their struggle against the government of President Omar Hassan al-Bashir.
Under the umbrella National Democratic Alliance (NDA), the gathering had been delayed several times since January.

The meeting opened in the absence of Sudan Peoples' Liberation Army (SPLA) leader John Garang, meant to have reached Asmara from the southern Sudan garrison of Yei. Garang was now expected in Asmara late on Monday or early Tuesday.

NDA president Mohamed Osman Al-Mirghani said: "This meeting has a special status as the struggle against the regime in Sudan is reaching its climax. The aim of this meeting is to unify all our efforts in the popular uprising against the regime."

"You have witnessed the escalation in the last few weeks of the war against the Bashir/(Hassan al-)Tourabi regime. Now the forces are about 40 miles (64 km) from Juba. This is a call to all armed forces in Sudan to change sides, to join the NDA and abandon support for the NIF regime," he told a news conference.
The SPLA, fighting towards the major southern town of Juba, said on Sunday it had captured an army garrison town on the Juba road.
"Lainya fell to the SPLA yesterday (Saturday)...," said SPLA Nairobi spokesman Samson Kwaje, adding that he received the news from SPLA leader Garang stationed in Yei.

In Khartoum, the Sudanese army said on Saturday it had lost contact with its units in Yei but would not say whether the town had fallen. Lainya, 100 km (63 miles) southwest of Juba, is 60 km (37 miles) northeast of Yei.
On Monday in Asmara, the SPLA said it had captured a huge quantity of arms, including 106 mm antitank guns, tanks and machine guns in Lainya.
The SPLA has been fighting Khartoum since 1983, demanding greater autonomy for the mainly-Christian and animist south of Sudan from the Moslem and Arabised north.

Al-Mirghani said all the rebels on the eastern and southern fronts in Sudan were Sudanese. "The "NIF (ruling Sudan party) says it is Eritrean, Ethiopian and Ugandan forces, but we clearly state it is Sudanese forces."
He said the gathering would focus on what he called the transitional period. He and former Sudan prime minister Sadiq al-Mahdi would present evaluations on the Sudan situation.
They will also seek ways to enhance opposition unity and how they would restructure Sudan when and if they won power.
